title: Accessible inverse images of full subcategories
statement: Fix a universe $\mathcal U$, with small Hom sets and small colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] relative to $\mathcal U$. A category is locally presentable if it is cocomplete and, for some infinite regular cardinal $\kappa\in\mathcal U$, generated under small $\kappa$-filtered colimits by a small set of objects whose Hom functors preserve those colimits. Here $\kappa$-filtered means every diagram with fewer than $\kappa$ morphisms has a cocone, and regular means a union of fewer than $\kappa$ sets of size less than $\kappa$ still has size less than $\kappa$. A replete full subcategory $\mathcal V\subseteq\mathcal D$ is accessible as a subcategory if, for some infinite regular $\lambda\in\mathcal U$, it is closed under small $\lambda$-filtered colimits in $\mathcal D$ and generated under these colimits by a small set of its objects; replete means closed under isomorphism in $\mathcal D$. Let $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal D$ be locally presentable categories and let $H:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ preserve small $\kappa$-filtered colimits for some infinite regular $\kappa\in\mathcal U$. Let $\mathcal V\subseteq\mathcal D$ be replete and accessible as a subcategory. Then the full subcategory $H^{-1}\mathcal V\subseteq\mathcal C$ on the objects $X$ for which $HX\in\mathcal V$ is replete and accessible as a subcategory. The cardinal witnessing the conclusion may differ from the cardinal for $H$ and from the cardinal for $\mathcal V$. The functor $H$ is arbitrary, including a functor between arrow categories that is not induced by a functor on their endpoint categories.

source.place: Corollary A.2.6.7, printed p. 820 (PDF p. 837), after enlargement to a common accessibility cardinal using Proposition A.2.6.5 Read online on 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this ordinary accessibility theorem.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal W=H^{-1}\mathcal V$. If $X\cong Y$ in $\mathcal C$ and $X\in\mathcal W$, applying $H$ to an isomorphism and its inverse gives $HX\cong HY$. Repleteness of $\mathcal V$ implies $HY\in\mathcal V$, hence $Y\in\mathcal W$. Thus $\mathcal W$ is replete.

source.place: Corollary A.2.6.7: repleteness of the inverse image

proof.text: Let $\lambda$ witness accessibility of $\mathcal V$. Apply [lem-coef-accessible-functor-presentability-ranks] to $H$ with $\alpha=\kappa$ and obtain $\rho\geq\kappa$. The forward direction of [lem-coef-accessible-subdiagram-criterion], applied to $\mathcal V\subseteq\mathcal D$ with $\sigma=\lambda$, gives its approximation property at every sufficiently large regular rank sharply above $\lambda$. Choose an infinite regular $\sigma\geq\rho,\lambda$, and use the arbitrary-large-rank clause of the rank theorem to choose a regular $\mu$ with $\sigma\ll\mu$ above that fixed bound. In particular $\lambda\ll\mu$ and $\rho\ll\mu$, since the exponent condition for $\sigma$ includes those for $\lambda$ and $\rho$. Both ambient categories are locally $\mu$-presentable. The moreover clause of the criterion now gives a small family generating $\mathcal V$ under $\mu$-filtered ambient colimits. These indices are also $\lambda$-filtered, so $\mathcal V$ is closed under them. Also $\mu\geq\kappa$, so $H$ preserves these colimits. We have obtained generation and closure at one common rank, rather than assuming generation survives an arbitrary cardinal enlargement.

source.place: Definitions A.2.6.2-3 and Proposition A.2.6.5, especially the generating-family conclusion in the first paragraph of its proof; common-rank preparation for Corollary A.2.6.7

proof.text: For any small $\mu$-filtered diagram $Y:I\to\mathcal W$, its ambient colimit $Y_I$ exists in $\mathcal C$. Preservation by $H$ identifies $H(Y_I)$ with $\operatorname{colim}_I HY$. Each $HY_i$ lies in $\mathcal V$, and its $\mu$-filtered colimit lies there by step 2. Repleteness therefore gives $H(Y_I)\in\mathcal V$, so $Y_I\in\mathcal W$. The comparison is the canonical one determined by the cocone maps in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Thus $\mathcal W$ is closed under these ambient colimits.

source.place: Corollary A.2.6.7: closure under the common-rank filtered colimits

proof.text: We prove the approximation condition for $\mathcal W$ at every sufficiently large infinite regular $\tau$ with $\mu\ll\tau$. Since $\rho\leq\mu$, the exponent definition gives $\rho\ll\tau$, and [lem-coef-accessible-functor-presentability-ranks] makes $H$ carry $\tau$-presentable objects to $\tau$-presentable objects. Take a small $\tau$-filtered poset $I$, a diagram $X:I\to\mathcal C$ of such objects, $X_I\in\mathcal W$, and $S\subseteq I$ of size less than $\tau$. The diagram $HX$ consists of $\tau$-presentable objects and has colimit isomorphic to $H(X_I)\in\mathcal V$, because $\tau\geq\kappa$. Apply [lem-coef-accessible-subdiagram-criterion] to $\mathcal V\subseteq\mathcal D$ at $\sigma=\mu$, using its closure and small generating family from step 2. For every sufficiently large such $\tau$, it supplies a subset $J\subseteq I$ containing $S$, of size less than $\tau$, which is $\mu$-filtered and for which $\operatorname{colim}_J HX_j\in\mathcal V$. The ambient colimit $X_J$ exists, and $\mu\geq\kappa$ gives $H(X_J)\cong\operatorname{colim}_J HX_j$. Repleteness yields $X_J\in\mathcal W$. All the bounds used depend only on the fixed categories, $H$ and $\mathcal V$, so this verifies the required condition uniformly for all $I,X,S$.

source.place: Proposition A.2.6.5, condition (2 prime) at tau, transferred through H to prove Corollary A.2.6.7

proof.text: The ambient category $\mathcal C$ is locally presentable, $\mathcal W$ is replete by step 1 and closed under small $\mu$-filtered ambient colimits by step 3. Step 4 proves condition (ii) of [lem-coef-accessible-subdiagram-criterion] for every sufficiently large regular $\tau$ with $\mu\ll\tau$. Its converse gives a small family generating $\mathcal W$ under small $\mu$-filtered ambient colimits. This generation together with closure is precisely accessibility as a subcategory in the statement. The rank $\mu$ was selected using both $H$ and $\mathcal V$. No step used an endpoint description of $H$, so the argument also applies to arbitrary functors between arrow categories.

source.place: Proposition A.2.6.5, converse; conclusion of Corollary A.2.6.7

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N9-62c3fa7c7 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, its five steps and the full statements of the cited nodes (presentability-ranks, subdiagram-criterion, category-colimit), and checked them against HTT A.2.6.2–A.2.6.7, printed pp. 818–820, from a local text of the PDF. HTT's A.2.6.7 claims accessibility at the same kappa without proof, and Lurie's warning before A.2.6.3 casts doubt on that. The item claims only accessibility at some rank. That is true, and it is what both citers (model-weak-equivalences-accessible, small-right-lifting-accessibility) use. Step 1 (repleteness) is elementary and correct. Step 2: the rank node with alpha=kappa gives rho; the criterion's forward direction for V at lambda gives a fixed bound; we choose sigma>=rho,lambda and then mu with sigma<<mu above that bound. sigma<<mu implies lambda<<mu and rho<<mu, so both categories are locally mu-presentable, and the moreover clause gives generation of V at mu. Since mu>kappa,lambda, V is closed under mu-filtered colimits and H preserves them. Step 3 (closure of W) is elementary and correct. Step 4: rho<=mu<<tau means H preserves tau-presentable objects. The criterion's forward direction for V at sigma=mu gives J, which is mu-filtered and nonempty, so H(X_J) is isomorphic to colim_J HX, and repleteness puts X_J in W. The bound does not depend on I, X or S. Step 5: the criterion's converse for W at mu holds, with all its hypotheses checked. Edge cases tested: V empty, V=D, H the identity, H constant (including an infinite constant), and V = infinite sets in Set; none breaks the statement. No new nodes; no cycle (the cited lemmas have empty proof_deps); everything cited is in the same unit or is a definition; no SGA; no tool_uses needed. A grep of Mathlib's Presentable/ and ObjectProperty/ found ObjectProperty.inverseImage instances but no inverse-image accessibility theorem, so no leaf is missed. The existing node lem-coef-accessible-arrow-inverse-image is a special case of this item, which is not a fault of this delivery. No changes made.

lean.statement: theorem accessible_full_inverse_image {C : Type u₁} {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v} C] [Category.{v} D] [IsLocallyPresentable.{v} C] [IsLocallyPresentable.{v} D] (κ : Cardinal.{v}) [Fact κ.IsRegular] (H : C ⥤ D) [H.IsCardinalAccessible κ] (V : ObjectProperty D) [V.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms] (hVacc : ∃ (lam : Cardinal.{v}) (_ : Fact lam.IsRegular), (∀ (J : Type v) (_ : SmallCategory J) (_ : IsCardinalFiltered J lam) (X : J ⥤ D), (∀ j, V (X.obj j)) → ∀ (c : Cocone X), Nonempty (IsColimit c) → V c.pt) ∧ ∃ (I : Type v) (P : I → D), (∀ i, V (P i)) ∧ ∀ (X : D), V X → ∃ (J : Type v) (_ : SmallCategory J) (_ : IsCardinalFiltered J lam) (Y : J ⥤ D) (c : Cocone Y), (∀ j, ∃ i, Nonempty (Y.obj j ≅ P i)) ∧ Nonempty (IsColimit c) ∧ Nonempty (c.pt ≅ X)) : ∃ (μ : Cardinal.{v}) (_ : Fact μ.IsRegular), (V.inverseImage H).IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms ∧ (∀ (J : Type v) (_ : SmallCategory J) (_ : IsCardinalFiltered J μ) (X : J ⥤ C), (∀ j, V (H.obj (X.obj j))) → ∀ (c : Cocone X), Nonempty (IsColimit c) → V (H.obj c.pt)) ∧ ∃ (I : Type v) (P : I → C), (∀ i, V (H.obj (P i))) ∧ ∀ (X : C), V (H.obj X) → ∃ (J : Type v) (_ : SmallCategory J) (_ : IsCardinalFiltered J μ) (Y : J ⥤ C) (c : Cocone Y), (∀ j, ∃ i, Nonempty (Y.obj j ≅ P i)) ∧ Nonempty (IsColimit c) ∧ Nonempty (c.pt ≅ X)
